metadata.title: आदिवासी विकास का प्रचार और हक़ीकत | Tribal Development: Publicity v/s Truth
metadata.description: The Modi government promised to revolutionize Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS), aimed at providing quality education to tribal children. Announcements included increasing the number of schools to 740 by 2026 and raising the annual expenditure per student from ₹61,000 to ₹1,09,000. However, these promises largely remain unfulfilled. As of now, many schools are incomplete, lacking proper infrastructure, teachers, and essential facilities like hostels, libraries, and labs. Reports highlight that students face overcrowded classrooms and poor living conditions, undermining the goal of bridging the education gap for tribal communities. The increased budget allocation on paper hasn’t translated to visible improvements on the ground. Critics argue that the scheme, originally envisioned to uplift tribal students by providing a nurturing academic environment, is falling short of its potential. This explainer breaks down the gaps between promises and reality, shedding light on why EMRS is still far from becoming the transformative initiative it was meant to be.
